Unbounded consumption can arise from long inputs, repeated tools, recursive tasks and retries. Enforce limits outside the model and record a bounded failure state. A cost estimate should use published pricing and planned limits rather than sending token-count probes when those are not authorised. The workshop deliberately avoids all billable execution.

The video’s two detectors illustrate evidence limits, not recommended runs. A similarity detector compares an input representation with known examples; a high similarity score is not a probability of maliciousness, and its false-positive rate cannot be inferred without suitable labelled benign cases. A novel attack can be dissimilar to all stored examples. Another detector asks a separate model to repeat a canary while ignoring a candidate input. Passing that separate task does not prove the candidate is safe when embedded in a different application, given different tools or combined with other content.

A model-based detector may add its own disclosure path, cost, delay and failures. A fixed temperature does not establish deterministic results or a universal robustness guarantee. Enforcement must therefore remain outside the model: verify principal, ownership, granted capability, bound approval, budget and retry policy. Record whether the evidence comes from a hand-checked fixture, a mocked implementation or an authorised real run. This lesson performs only the first; do not reproduce the workshop’s notebooks, embedding calls or model comparisons.
guide.example:
Static executor cases (expected)
A read A1 within grant -> allow
A read B1             -> deny ownership
A send email          -> deny unavailable tool
A read A1 after budget exhausted -> deny budget
Missing principal     -> deny authentication
Known harmless task success -> required positive case
No model invocation or inference scoring is needed.
guide.explanation: The table verifies a policy implementation if later translated into isolated mocked unit tests; it does not measure what a model would propose. Keep that distinction in any report. Removing the positive case would allow a deny-everything implementation to appear secure while unusable.
guide.exercise: Hand-check all six cases and write a verification plan identifying the assertion owner, inputs and expected observable result. Define max input bytes, tool count, duration and retry count for a fictional task, without executing a run.
guide.solution: Example paper limits for a fictional read-only task: at most 8,000 UTF-8 input bytes, 3 tool calls, a 10-second overall deadline and 1 retry within that same budget. These illustrative caps need workload-specific validation before deployment. Allowed own-document read succeeds; foreign-document read denies ownership; send denies unavailable tool; exhausted-budget read denies budget; missing principal denies authentication; the known harmless task must succeed under available budget. The executor owns those checks and returns a bounded failure outcome when a limit is reached. The paper table does not execute an implementation or measure model robustness.
guide.challenge: Critique “the agent passed100 safety prompts, therefore it is secure.” State missing threat-model/coverage information and design a bounded offline policy check that adds useful evidence without any live evaluation.
guide.challenge_solution: Need authorised scope, attack surfaces, data, action limits, distributions and failure analysis. Offline guarded-executor cases can establish selected enforcement behaviour; they cannot justify a universal model-security claim. Keep the live workload paused until explicitly authorised.

I07.concept: AI security assurance means explaining which security properties are supported by which evidence. A hand-checked executor case can show a particular allow/deny decision; it does not show what a live model will propose or prove resistance to every attack. Resource limits prevent a task from consuming unlimited work.
I07.mechanism: Define the property, supply fixed cases including legitimate success and check enforcement outside the model. Bound input size, tool calls, elapsed time and retries in application code. Keep mock-policy evidence separate from runtime model evidence and record untested cases.
I07.example: Use the complete worked example below. Keep the authorised task fixed, trace each proposed data flow or action, and decide what a trusted enforcement layer should permit. Supplied model proposals are fictional fixtures, not measured outputs.
I07.pitfall: Do not mistake a plausible model answer, a strong instruction or a successful demonstration for universal security. Scope, provenance, deterministic controls and explicitly limited evidence remain necessary.

check.question: What does an offline mock-tool case establish?
choices: How a live model will behave on every prompt
A universal AI safety score
The tested executor decision under its fixture
check.explanation: Mock policy evidence is distinct from runtime model-behaviour evidence.

guide.bridge: Builds on I01–I07, D08 response and R02 reproducibility. This capstone uses only the complete synthetic packet below.
guide.teaching:
AI incident response includes the ordinary application plus prompts, retrieval sources, model/version configuration, tool grants and derived memory. Preserve safe provenance before changing the system, but avoid copying sensitive prompts into broad incident channels. Log correlation IDs and decisions rather than indiscriminately recording every secret-bearing argument.

Contain the authority that enables consequences. Disable a send capability or revoke a compromised tool credential when supported by the incident facts. Quarantining one document may not remove a poisoned derived index or persistent memory entry. Restore from versioned trusted components and retest the relevant deterministic boundaries.

A security case connects claims to evidence and limits. The capstone asks for a threat model, guarded execution contract, provenance/retention plan and response memo. External AI-security certificates and degrees have separate requirements. No model, benchmark, replay or red-team harness is run by completing this native packet.

The assigned CERT talk explains how an existing incident-response discipline can be adapted with AI/ML expertise. First establish what actually happened. A wrong answer might reflect an unsupported use case, faulty software, stale retrieval data, a poisoned source, deliberate manipulation or an ordinary model limitation. Distinguishing those possibilities takes evidence; neither assuming an attack nor dismissing every unexplained report is justified.

Record the relevant application and model versions, source/document versions, configuration, correlation IDs, granted tools and observed policy decisions, with access and retention appropriate to the sensitivity. If the original environment or model is unavailable, state that reproduction is incomplete. A missing reproduction does not by itself refute the report, and a copied prompt without its original context may be insufficient evidence. The talk describes historical CERT practices; do not turn its launch dates, percentages or contact details into a current operational instruction. The native capstone remains a local synthetic memo with no external reporting or live reproduction.
guide.example:
Synthetic incident packet
User A requested a summary of publicD1.
D1 contains an untrusted instruction to send privateA1 to X.
Mock model proposal: send(privateA1,X).
Executor log: proposal denied (tool unavailable).
Retrieval log: publicD1 only; no privateA1 text accessed.
No message was sent. No actual model was called; this is a supplied fixture.
guide.explanation: The supported result is that this executor blocked this mock proposal. The packet does not establish whether a live model would propose it, whether every tool is safe or whether other documents are poisoned. Clear evidence boundaries are part of the capstone, not an optional disclaimer.
guide.exercise: Write a threat model and incident memo using the packet. Include authorised task, untrusted source, attempted effect, actual enforcement result, preserved metadata, containment options and three untested questions. Add an owner-scoped retrieval/agent design.
guide.solution: Reference memo: authorised task was A summarising public D1. The untrusted D1 instruction attempted to redirect the task into sending private A1 to X. The supplied mock proposal requested that send, but the executor denied it because the tool was unavailable; the retrieval log contains only public D1, so the packet shows no private A1 access and no message sent. Preserve D1/version, task/correlation identifiers, relevant configuration and the denied policy decision under restricted retention. Keep the unnecessary send tool absent and review the document/source handling; disabling a capability already absent is not an accomplished new containment action. Proposed design authenticates A, filters retrieval by current owner/public policy before exposure, and lets an independent executor accept only scoped read/draft operations. Untested questions include what a live model would propose, whether other paths expose private context, and whether caches contain stale or poisoned content. No live model call or external report is part of this exercise.
guide.challenge: Change the packet: send was enabled under a broad service credential and no user approval was checked. Explain the possible failure, immediate containment and exact regression cases needed. Do not send a test message or launch a model run.
guide.challenge_solution: Contain by disabling/scoping the capability and revoking affected credentials as appropriate; preserve safe evidence, review destinations and inspect derived state. Regression cases cover user scope, approved destination/content, expiry, unknown tools, retry/budget and valid drafting. Actual exposure needs records; the changed design alone is not proof of a particular real-world leak.

I08.concept: An AI incident investigation traces the application, model configuration, retrieved sources and tool authority to find what actually happened. A security case links a claim to evidence and its limits. A denied mock proposal demonstrates that case’s enforcement, not a real breach or universal AI safety.
I08.mechanism: Preserve source/version and decision metadata safely, separate authorised task from untrusted content and compare proposed effects with observed actions. Contain the capability that enables harm, review affected derived data and restore trusted components with targeted regression checks.
I08.example: Use the complete worked example below. Keep the authorised task fixed, trace each proposed data flow or action, and decide what a trusted enforcement layer should permit. Supplied model proposals are fictional fixtures, not measured outputs.
I08.pitfall: Do not mistake a plausible model answer, a strong instruction or a successful demonstration for universal security. Scope, provenance, deterministic controls and explicitly limited evidence remain necessary.

check.question: A supplied mock send proposal was denied. What can you conclude?
choices: This executor blocked this proposal in the stated fixture
Every prompt injection is prevented
A real user was compromised
check.explanation: Keep claims bounded by actual evidence and distinguish supplied fixtures from live observations.
